summary: STORE-012D CONCEPT PULSE™ verified end-to-end. Backend: 9/9 pytest PASS, 1 skipped (no_shared_set branch — pre-existing /public/journeys/initiate 500 bug from iter174, unrelated). Critical invariants enforced: (a) GET /api/journeys/{jid}/concept-pulse response body NEVER contains the substring 'client_alignment_score' — string-scanned the raw HTTP response text; (b) ranking rows emit only alignment_band ∈ {high,medium,low} + alignment_label ∈ {'High alignment','Medium alignment','Low alignment'}; (c) read-only — snapshotted moodboard.status across the 3 boards of the latest set before+after the GET, identical; (d) ranking sort is band-bucketed (high→medium→low) with weighted reactions tie-break (preferred=10·comment=5·interested=3·explore_further=2); (e) suggested_next_action key for the test journey is 'develop_preferred' (preferred=B9 Elegant Warm Contemporary exists, no material keyword in comments) with headline 'Develop Elegant Warm Contemporary with material variants'; (f) quick_actions[] contains open_preferred (/moodboards/{mb_id}), material_board_preferred, generate_alternatives (kind='api', method=POST), view_feedback (/client/journey/{jid}/concepts). Regression: list endpoint and client concept-directions endpoint still pass, and client endpoint never leaks 'client_alignment_score'. Frontend: ConceptPulseCard renders inside /studio/journey/{jid} on Phase 2 of 7 (INSPIRE) at data-testid=jop-concept-pulse-block — confirmed via Playwright after admin login (admin@moodfordesign.com/Blueprint2024! → /dashboard → navigated to journey). Visual capture shows: 'Concept Pulse™' header + 'DIRECTION SET 09' badge · SUGGESTED NEXT MOVE block with the correct headline · CLIENT PREFERRED DIRECTION strip 'Elegant Warm Contemporary' + Open CTA · Ranking #1 Warm Scandinavian / #2 Elegant Warm Contemporary / #3 Warm Timeless Classic, every row labelled 'MEDIUM ALIGNMENT' (no raw 11/13/23 numbers visible) · Feedback Summary chips Interesting 1 · Explore Further 0 · Preferred 2 · Comments 1 · Quick Actions row with all 4 buttons. CRITICAL UI INVARIANT holds: no 'score' substring and no integer adjacent to 'alignment' rendered in the card.

critical_code_review_comments: concept_directions.py is now 1068 LOC — well over the 700-line target. The STORE-012D block (lines 825-1068, ~243 LOC) is self-contained and easily extractable into routers/concept_pulse.py (its only shared dep is _resolve_journey, _reaction_counts and _now). Recommend splitting before STORE-012E lands.

_band() / _BAND_LABEL / _ALIGNMENT_BANDS thresholds live as module constants. If thresholds ever need per-tenant tuning (e.g. higher bar for premium clients), pull them into tenant_settings. Acceptable today but worth a comment.

_comment_mentions_material uses a flat tuple of 24 keywords with substring 'in' matching — false positives possible (e.g. a comment 'material is fine' triggers material_board even if client meant something else). Consider word-boundary regex (\b{kw}\b) for cleaner detection.

Ranking tie-break uses direction_letter as final key — when set_index >= 2 letters become A2/B2/C2 which sort alphabetically as expected, but A11/B11 vs A2 would sort wrong if any journey ever reaches 10+ sets. Low priority but consider zero-padding the letter suffix or breaking on shared_at instead.

Response is fully computed every request — no caching. For the journey page this fires on every render/navigation. If the page polls or revalidates, consider a 30s stale-while-revalidate to reduce DB load. Optional.

STORE-012D invariant 'never leak client_alignment_score' is enforced only by code inspection — there is no schema-level guard. The pytest string-scan in test_iter219 acts as the regression net; keep this test in CI to catch future code paths that might naively spread `**seed` into the response.

Frontend ConceptPulseCard not inspected directly (only rendered output verified); but the data-testid scheme (concept-pulse, cp-suggested-action, cp-preferred, cp-ranking, cp-feedback-summary, cp-quick-actions, cp-qa-{key}) is consistent with prior cards and lets future tests target every section without fragile text selectors.
